DXd.bystander_effect: High (uncharged payload readily diffuses across membranes)
absolute_contraindications: Active or pre-existing drug-induced interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis
monitoring_requirements: Prompt high-resolution CT chest upon any cough, dyspnea, or fever
Periodic baseline and on-treatment echocardiogram / MUGA scan for LVEF
drug_interactions: Concomitant cardiotoxic or pulmonary toxic agents
Strong OATP1B1/1B3 or P-gp modulators (minimal clinical impact relative to systemic organ reserve)

DM1.bystander_effect: Low/negligible (charged lysosomal catabolite lysine-MCC-DM1 remains trapped in targeted cell)
primary_toxicities: Thrombocytopenia (frequent Grade 3-4, risk of fatal intracranial/GI bleeding)
absolute_contraindications: Baseline platelet count < 100,000/uL prior to initiation
Severe hepatic impairment (total bilirubin > 3x ULN or AST/ALT > 5x ULN without hepatic metastases)
monitoring_requirements: Platelet count and CBC prior to each treatment cycle
Hepatic transaminases (AST, ALT) and total bilirubin prior to each cycle
LVEF evaluation at baseline and every 3 months
drug_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole) increase DM1 exposure; avoid concomitant use
Anticoagulants or antiplatelet therapies markedly increase hemorrhage risk with thrombocytopenia

MMAE.bystander_effect: High (neutral hydrophobic payload diffuses into adjacent cells upon cathepsin B cleavage)
primary_toxicities: Severe hyperglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis (in Padcev / Nectin-4 constructs)
Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCAR, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, TEN)
absolute_contraindications: Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C) - MMAE clearance is primarily biliary/hepatic
Active Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis
monitoring_requirements: Screen for numbness, tingling, weakness (neuropathy dose delays or reductions)
Frequent blood glucose monitoring in diabetic patients receiving enfortumab vedotin
Inspect skin for progressive rash or bullous lesions
Monitor renal reserve (CrCl < 30 mL/min associated with higher mortality/toxicities)
drug_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, clarithromycin, voriconazole) markedly increase free MMAE AUC and toxicity; close monitoring or dose reduction required
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, St. John's wort) decrease MMAE efficacy

SN-38.mechanism: Topoisomerase I inhibitor (active metabolite of irinotecan)
SN-38.bystander_effect: Moderate to high (pH-sensitive cleavable linker releases free SN-38 in tumor microenvironment)
primary_toxicities: Severe, life-threatening neutropenia and febrile neutropenia
Severe diarrhea (early and late onset, dehydration and electrolyte collapse)
absolute_contraindications: Severe uncontrolled neutropenia (ANC < 1500/uL at cycle initiation)
Severe hepatic impairment (bilirubin > 1.5x ULN without documented Gilbert syndrome)
monitoring_requirements: Test for UGT1A1*28 genotype: homozygous (*28/*28) patients have impaired glucuronidation clearance and substantially higher risk of severe neutropenia and diarrhea; require reduced starting dose or intensified monitoring
Active monitoring for early/late diarrhea; immediate high-dose loperamide protocol
CBC with differential prior to each dose
drug_interactions: UGT1A1 inhibitors (e.g., atazanavir, gemfibrozil, ketoconazole) increase SN-38 exposure
UGT1A1 inducers (e.g., rifampin, phenytoin) decrease SN-38 exposure

general_prescribing_rules.elderly_renal_cutoff: CrCl < 30 mL/min requires dose adjustment and close toxicodynamic surveillance for auristatin and maytansinoid ADCs.
general_prescribing_rules.elderly_hepatic_cutoff: Child-Pugh B or C leads to profound drug accumulation of lipophilic payloads (MMAE, DM1, SN-38) cleared hepatically.
general_prescribing_rules.polypharmacy_cyp3a4: Concomitant administration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with MMAE or DM1 triggers an mandatory drug-interaction alert and clinician review.
general_prescribing_rules.novelty_unverified_rule: If an ADC construct, target pairing, or clinical trial number is not documented in verified databases (openFDA, ADCDB, ClinicalTrials.gov), the agent MUST abstain (verdict: dont_know, needs_human: true).
